page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory capacity is configured at 192.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in CPU-intensive tasks. The server achieves top 10% placement in Passmark CPU scores, single-threaded gzip compression at 36.54 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 575.95 GB/sec. It also demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities with a stress-ng multi-core score of 95440.36 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 18336.0. Cryptographic and vector operations are highly accelerated, supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 333.72 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D96ls_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. It avoids the premium cost of unneeded memory while delivering high-density processing power. This makes the instance highly suitable for software compilation, static web serving, cryptographic processing, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing, where it achieves 304.72 tokens/sec on medium 7B models.
